text: Just one single button inside Power BI Desktop actually triggers publishing — but it's genuinely worth understanding everything that one button sets in motion behind the scenes.
File, then Publish, then Publish to Power BI. Sign in if you're prompted to, and that's the entire first step, done in a matter of seconds.
Search for and select the exact workspace you're publishing into — any workspace where you already hold Contributor access or higher shows up right here in this search box, ready to pick.

When publishing finishes, you get a direct link straight to the newly created report. Publishing itself creates both a semantic model and a report, and both of them carry the exact same name as your original Desktop file.

Republishing is genuinely where the real risk lives, so pay close attention here. Duplicate semantic model names in the same workspace can break the whole republish outright. Renaming or deleting a field that a visual in the service already depends on will break that visual immediately. And republishing kicks off an immediate refresh right away, layered right on top of whatever scheduled refresh you already had configured.

Power BI's impact analysis warns you first, showing exactly how many workspaces, reports, and dashboards your change could actually affect before you ever confirm the overwrite. Lesson 71 goes much deeper into exactly what that published semantic model actually is, underneath all of this.
